endorsements.quote: Since batch effects are inescapable, developers should know that testing the model on new batches is a better practice than merging multiple batches and then splitting the merged dataset into training and test sets (like in a cross validation).
To establish credibility, it must be compared against cutting edge tools, AI-based or not, for clearer performance evaluation and value-add.
Users should be informed about the data the model was trained on, and the limits of the model, such as which sublabels do not work well.
To apply tip 7, developers must calibrate the reported accuracy of a model tested with an artificially balanced dataset in accordance with real-world class-label proportions.
When applying tip 10, a developer should use multiple relevant datasets especially during validation to ensure that the model is likely to generalize.

unlisted_practices: Curate validation data to include sufficient problems at varying levels of difficulty, not predominantly easy cases.
Report model performance stratified by difficulty level rather than only as an overall score.
Include closely similar cross-class samples in training and test sets to reveal superficial learning.
Benchmark model performance against null models, such as randomly generated feature sets, and report significance.
Use prior knowledge and convergent validation for feature selection rather than relying only on the data.
Do not artificially balance test sets; users should recalibrate reported metrics to real-world class prevalence.
Ensure models decline to predict when new batches are too different from the training distribution.
Check for test-set bias arising from cross-sample normalization.
Share code openly to improve reproducibility.
Users should validate a model using a new batch of their own data and compare results with reported performance.

screen.reason: This is a guidance/tips article providing recommendations on how developers and users can ensure ML model validity in biomedical and healthcare contexts.
